In this video, we will explore
the toolbars available in Altium Designer
and how they are context sensitive

so that only commands
that are relevant to the document of focus
are available.

With the schematic
as the active document,
select the View menu.

Select Toolbars
to observe the tools that are available.

If there is a checkmark to the left
of the tool name,
then it will be visible.

These are the classic toolbars
available in Altium Designer.

Hover the cursor over any icon
to see the description of each tool.

Classic toolbars can be moved
and rearranged within Altium Designer,
as shown,

by clicking the beginning
of the toolbar and dragging it.

Classic toolbars can also be left
floating, as shown.

Observe the icons
at the top of the design space.
This is called the Active Toolbar.

It allows for quick access
to frequently used functions

that are also found in the main menus
and in a classic toolbar.

You can hover over any icon
to view a pop-up of the icons description.
Left-click on an icon to select that command.
For placement commands,
the object will appear on the cursor.

When there is a white triangle displayed
in the bottom right corner of an icon

there is a group of additional
similar icons available.
Left-click and hold

or right-click to view the additional icons
available for that group.
Like menus and other options,

the toolbars within Altium Designer
are context sensitive.

If the focused document type changes
so will the toolbar icons.

Altium Designer automatically adjusts
the toolbar icons

to suit the type of document
that is opened.

For example,
the schematic and PCB documents
require different types of operations.
In the schematic,
wires and symbols are placed.
While in the PCB,
trace routes and components are placed.

In this video, we explored the toolbars
available in Altium Designer

and explained how they
are context sensitive.
